first_impression.summary_in_own_words: It's a planner that will organise a wedding for us somewhere in the US or Canada, Hawaii, Napa, New York, Banff, and someone called a Wedded Advisor plans it with us. The top is mostly about Hawaii marriage licence rules, which I didn't expect to be the first thing I read.

attention_map.quote: Hawaii is the simplest legal example: no residency rule, and no waiting period once your licence is issued.
attention_map.why: Good to know it's actually legal for us, but at 10pm I wanted to see what it looks like and roughly what it costs, not licence rules in the second line. 'pairs you with a Wedded Advisor who plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance' is the line that kept me going.
Five quick taps and our guest number is actually an option. Feels like someone has thought about a group our size. I'd tap through it but I don't know what 'Check your date' does yet.

attention_map.quote: Legal and entry rules from official government sites, checked October 2026.
attention_map.why: Fine, but that tells me about the rules, not about them. It's not a reason to trust this company with our wedding.

attention_map.quote: A second-line parade walking your guests through New Orleans.
attention_map.why: This is the bit I'd screenshot for my partner. Lake Louise frozen in winter and the New Orleans second line feel different from every Bali and Italy page. Some lines drift into brochure talk though: 'the city that never needs a backdrop', 'slow gold late afternoons'.

attention_map.quote: Las Vegas suits a quick, glamorous ceremony; Nevada sets its own licence rules, and your Wedded Advisor checks them before you book flights.
attention_map.why: Vegas is one we're actually weighing up, so I'm glad it's here and not treated as a joke. Short, but it's there.

attention_map.quote: Rules set by California; we check them for your date
attention_map.why: On my phone a five-column table is a sideways scroll. The legal column says the same thing seven times, so it reads like filler. The 'fit' column is the useful bit: 'Couples and small groups' for Las Vegas, 'Large family weeks' for Maui. But nothing tells me how many people a place can take, how long the flight is from Sydney, or what any of it costs.

attention_map.quote: Collect the licence no sooner than 30 days before the ceremony. There is no waiting period once it is issued
attention_map.why: Clear, numbered, and with an official source. It tells me we both have to turn up in person, which matters when we're flying in from Australia.

attention_map.quote: Check ESTA eligibility on the official US site before flying to the US, and check eTA rules on the official Canadian site before flying to Canada.
attention_map.why: US passports are listed first, then UK, and we come last. The US and UK lines give an actual answer. Ours just tells us to go and look it up ourselves. Our guests are nearly all Australian, so the one line that's about us is the vague one.

attention_map.quote: Tell us your month and we check weather, rates and availability for it.
attention_map.why: I wanted to know when to go, and it just tells me to ask.

attention_map.quote: Where should we even start? ... How do we plan from overseas?
attention_map.why: These are literally my questions, word for word. The overseas guide link is what I'd tap. Then 'What will it cost?' only takes me to an FAQ that doesn't give a number.

attention_map.quote: Ishita and Devin's cultural wedding in Toronto
attention_map.why: Real couples is what I want to see. But there's no detail here, no guest numbers or where they came from, and 'A fairy-tale wedding in Hawaii' is the vaguest title of the lot, for the place I'm most interested in.

attention_map.quote: Milestone birthday: a wine country weekend in Napa
Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact: they explain your options, the legal route for your passports and what drives cost.
attention_map.why: One contact is exactly what I want so we're not juggling suppliers across time zones. The steps make sense. 'Travel, rooms and a guest website' is the only place that touches on where our guests stay, and it's one line.

attention_map.quote: Marketplace: Browse partner venues and suppliers in the United States and Canada, and send every enquiry through Wedded Concierge.
attention_map.why: So is it a planner or a directory? If I browse myself, am I still getting the advisor? This made me less sure what I'm actually signing up for.

attention_map.quote: Viral weddings, from K-pop royalty to Napa Valley romance
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip on a planning page. The Las Vegas and Hawaii posts I might save. The trending bit makes it feel like a magazine.

attention_map.quote: A realistic budget depends on four things: the place, the season, your guest count and how far your guests fly.
attention_map.why: I asked if our budget is realistic and got told it depends. Then the Hawaii one says 'the total depends on what you choose', which is exactly what makes me think the price will blow out. The just-the-two-of-us and legal answers are clear and useful.

attention_map.quote: Tell us the place, month and guest count, even if nothing is fixed yet.
attention_map.why: Long list of fields, but only name and email are required, and 'even if nothing is fixed yet' is reassuring for someone at a 2 out of 10. 'A Wedded Advisor replies' doesn't say who or when.

questions_answered.question: What does this cost all in, and what is included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: No price anywhere. The cost route in 'Start with the question you actually have' goes to the FAQ, which says 'A realistic budget depends on four things'. Even the Hawaii licence fee line says 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current state fee'.

questions_answered.question: Can it fit our guest count?
questions_answered.evidence: Guest bands in the router and form include '31 to 80', and the table gives rough fit notes ('Large family weeks or adults-only resort stays', 'Couples and small groups'). No numbers for any place or venue.

questions_answered.question: Who would actually plan this with us, and what do they do?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact' plus five steps in 'See how planning with us works'. I know what the role does, not who the person is.

questions_answered.question: How do our guests get there and where do they stay?
questions_answered.evidence: Australian entry line is only 'Check ESTA eligibility on the official US site'. FAQ says 'both countries are long-haul'. No flight times from Australia. Accommodation is one line: 'Travel, rooms and a guest website so everyone knows where to be.'

questions_answered.question: Is our budget realistic for this place?
questions_answered.evidence: The budget FAQ lists drivers only and sends me to the form: 'your Wedded Advisor talks you through what drives the cost'.

objections_triggered.objection: I don't know if my budget is possible for this many people
objections_triggered.triggered_by: "A realistic budget depends on four things: the place, the season, your guest count and how far your guests fly."

objections_triggered.objection: Prices look like they start low and will blow out
objections_triggered.triggered_by: "it means the total depends on what you choose" (Hawaii all-inclusive FAQ)

objections_triggered.objection: This page is written for Americans, not for Australians flying in
objections_triggered.triggered_by: US passports listed first everywhere, "For a mostly American guest list..." in the FAQ, and the Australian travel line is the only one that says 'check on the official site' instead of giving an answer

objections_triggered.objection: Planning from overseas, time zones and suppliers I can't meet
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Partly eased by "Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact" and the 'plan a wedding in the USA from overseas' link, but the Marketplace card ('Browse partner venues and suppliers') makes me wonder if I end up dealing with suppliers myself

objections_triggered.objection: Every planner's page looks the same
objections_triggered.triggered_by: "the city that never needs a backdrop", "slow gold late afternoons" and the trending K-pop article

trust_signals_noticed: Official sources with check dates (Hawaii Department of Health, NYC City Clerk, US State Department)
Real weddings named by couple and city
One named role as the single contact, with five planning steps
Our guest band '31 to 80' offered as an option
'Elopements and small weddings are welcome' and 'even if nothing is fixed yet'
turn_offs_noticed: Some brochure adjectives in the spotlight ('slow gold late afternoons', 'the city that never needs a backdrop')
Wide comparison table that will be a sideways scroll on my phone
Long form field list, softened by only name and email being required

emotional_response.excited_by: Lake Louise in winter, the New Orleans second line, Vegas taken seriously
emotional_response.reassured_by: Hawaii legal steps and having one contact person
emotional_response.uneasy_about: Cost, and feeling like the page treats Australians as an afterthought
emotional_response.overall: Interested enough to send it to my partner, not confident enough to fill in the form tonight

payload.decision_reason: I'd save this and send it to my partner because the Hawaii legal steps, the Vegas mention and the 'one contact' line make it feel doable. I won't enquire yet. Two of my five questions aren't answered at all (what it costs, and whether our budget is realistic), and the travel answers for us as Australians are the vaguest on the page: 'check ESTA eligibility on the official US site', no flight times from Sydney, and one line about where guests stay. Known gaps also decided it: no from price with inclusions and no named person who'd plan it, which is what I need before I hand over my details.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Ooh, Lake Louise frozen in winter, and a brass band walking everyone through New Orleans, that's different. Sending that bit to my partner. Good to know Hawaii is legal for us without hanging around for ages. But I still have no idea if 60 people in Maui is a 40k wedding or a 150k wedding, and the bit for Australian passports basically says google it. Why are we third after Americans and Brits? Saving it, will look properly on the weekend.
